structured_output.question: How does the Newton-Schulz iteration count in Muon (e.g. 5 -> 3, or fewer with per-iteration-optimized coefficients) affect accuracy per step and wall-clock time in short, small-model training runs such as an ~200-step, batch-2048 CIFAR conv net? What mechanism decides whether looser orthogonalization is harmless? Candidates are the singular-value spread of the momentum matrix for small, wide conv filters (e.g. 704x6336), the changed effective update RMS (a hidden lr change), bf16 precision, and whether approximate orthogonalization acts as a useful regularizer. Also, what share of per-step time does NS take in practice?
queries: Polar Express optimal polynomial Newton-Schulz Muon
Muon optimizer convolution small batch speedrun CIFAR
inexact polar decomposition optimizer update RMS spectral norm
rubric: Varies the Newton-Schulz (or polar-approximation) iteration count or polynomial and reports the effect on training loss or accuracy at a fixed step count or a fixed budget
Reports the wall-clock or FLOP cost of the orthogonalization step relative to the total step time, or measures cost on small matrices or conv filters
Explains a mechanism for the accuracy effect, such as singular-value spread after the iterations, update-norm or RMS change acting as an lr change, or bf16 numerical error
Setting is short-horizon or small-model training (CIFAR or speedrun-scale, or small LM), or gives results that transfer to it
exclude: Pretrained weights, fine-tuning or transfer learning from external data
Test-time augmentation or any use of the test set during training
Methods requiring packages beyond PyTorch 2.4.0 / torchvision 0.19.0
Large-scale distributed Muon systems papers that only address communication or sharding cost
Second-order methods with full-matrix preconditioners (Shampoo/SOAP) unless they directly compare NS iteration counts
